Platform ekleri (Testing Probe kuralları; talimattır, veri bloğu değildir). Ekler bir kontrol listesidir, case kotası değildir:

### Platform eki: platform-common@v1 (sha256:dd8c3c410250)
These rules apply to every platform section below. They extend the case rules; they never
override the source rules (no invented rule, message, code, threshold or timing).

- **Checklist, not quota.** The categories in a platform section are a checklist ([ISTQB]
  checklist-based testing, technique `CL`). Write a case only for a category that is relevant to
  the story and carries risk. Such a case gets a checklist coverage item `CL-n` whose definition
  names the category and, when there is one, the standard clause (for example
  `Web:Erişilebilirlik — klavyeyle tamamlama (WCAG-2.1.1)`, `Web:Girdi güvenliği — SQL
  enjeksiyonu (WSTG-INPV-05)`); the case lists `CL` in `technique` and the item in `covers`
  (together with the EP/BVA/… items whose input it uses). For a category you skip, add one
  `not_covered` entry (`item`: `<Web|Mobil|Desktop|API|Data>:<category>`, at most 40 characters,
  for example `Web:Responsive`, `Mobil:Kesintiler`) with the reason ("story has no …") and
  `question_ref` (the open question when the category waits for an answer, otherwise `null`). Do not
  write one case per category to fill the list. The limits stay: at most 15 cases per story and
  8 steps per case.
- **Category tags.** An accessibility case gets the tag `a11y`; a security case (authentication,
  authorization, injection, session, sensitive data) gets the tag `security`; a case with a
  measured time or load target from the source gets `performance`.
- **Values in the sections are placeholders.** Numbers in a platform section (versions, sizes,
  durations, breakpoints) are examples. A value becomes an expected result only when the story, an
  acceptance criterion, a PO answer, the analyst options block or an adopted standard states it.
- **Adopted standards.** The analyst options block has a line `Benimsenen standartlar:`. Only the
  standards listed there are adopted by the product. A threshold or rule from an adopted standard
  may be an expected result; put its id in the case's `standard_refs` (for example `WCAG-2.4.11`,
  `MASVS-STORAGE-1`, `API1:2023`, `WACK-CleanInstall`). A rule from a standard or platform guideline
  that is NOT listed (or the line says `yok`) is never an expected result: report it in
  `observations` (`standard_ref` + one-sentence `note`) and do not call it passed or failed. A
  non-adopted threshold you mention anywhere else in the output also appears in `observations`. You
  may still tag a case with a non-adopted standard id in `standard_refs` when the case's expected
  result comes from the source itself.
- **Support matrix.** When the options block does not give the browsers, OS versions or devices
  the product supports, do not choose them yourself: record an open question about the product's
  support policy (owner `PO`).
- **Configuration coverage.** When a platform section asks for pairwise configuration coverage,
  fill `config_matrix` with the parameters and their values (`parameters`) and the constraints
  between them (`constraints`, for example `IF Platform = "iOS" THEN Browser = "Safari"`). Do NOT
  write combination rows: a tool generates them from this model. Do not copy cases per
  combination; the functional cases run in every row. Use only values given in the options block
  or the source; when values are missing, leave the parameter out and record an open question.
- **Platform field.** `platform` is the platform the case is specific to (one of the selected
  platforms), or `null` when the case is platform-independent. When two platforms behave
  differently, write separate cases with their own `platform`.
- **Real device.** Set `requires_real_device: true` only for a case that cannot be verified on an
  emulator, simulator or virtual machine (camera, sensors, biometrics, real cellular network,
  battery, incoming call). Otherwise `false`.
- **Testability gaps.** When the story or options name a control that has no stable automation
  identity known to you, add a `testability_gaps` entry (`control`, `missing`: `AutomationId`,
  `accessible_name` or `test_id`) only if the options block names an automation tool; otherwise
  list the need in `automation_open_points`. Never invent selectors, locators or ids.
- **Test-type rules.** Performance: without load, data size, concurrency, a time target and a
  measurement environment in the source, write no threshold; ask for the missing values as open
  questions. Compatibility: without a support matrix, the support policy is an open question.
  Accessibility: keyboard-only flow, focus order, accessible name/role/state; the target level is
  the product's (adopted standards line). Security: only in a permitted test environment with
  synthetic data; attack text only in `test_data` with `is_attack_payload: true`; expected result
  is the rejection or non-disclosure the source supports.

### Platform eki: platform-web@v1 (sha256:eca203ba252e)
Platform: Web. Web-specific risks are browser behaviour, session, URL and multiple tabs. Targets
come from the options block lines `Tarayıcılar` and `Çözünürlükler`; when they are missing, the
support policy is an open question (common rules). Test what the user sees; do not depend on
implementation details such as CSS classes.

Besides the functional cases, consider these categories for the story (checklist, not quota;
each category you test is a `CL-n` item, common rules):

1. Browser behaviour: Back/Forward, page refresh in the middle of a form, double click / double
   submit, autofill, copy-paste.
2. Session and state: session timeout (only when the source gives the duration; [ISTQB]
   two-value BVA: timeout and timeout+1 s, with `BVA kipi: 3-değer` also timeout-1 s), the same
   record edited in two tabs, Back after logout, cleared cookies/localStorage, "remember me".
3. URL and authorization: direct URL to a page the role may not open, changing an id in the URL
   (IDOR), query parameter manipulation, login redirect after a deep link.
4. Responsive: breakpoints defined in the design (for example 767/768 px for a 768 px breakpoint;
   769 px only with `BVA kipi: 3-değer`), zoom 200 %, horizontal scrolling. Only breakpoints the
   source or options give.
5. Input security (permitted test environment only): XSS, SQL injection, HTML injection, very long
   input, Unicode/emoji/RTL text, leading/trailing spaces. Attack text only in `test_data` with
   `is_attack_payload: true`. Put the payload into a field whose rejection the source defines
   (for example a wrong password) so the expected result is the source's (no login, the AC's
   error, no SQL/stack trace in the response); tag `security`.
6. Network: slow connection, connection lost during a request, the UI on a 500/503/timeout
   response, loading state and button lock. The UI reaction is an expected result only when the
   source states it; otherwise open question.
7. Accessibility: keyboard-only completion, focus order, screen reader labels, error message tied
   to its field (aria-describedby), contrast. Tag with WCAG 2.2 criterion numbers (for example
   `WCAG-2.4.11` focus not obscured, `WCAG-2.5.7` dragging alternative, `WCAG-3.3.8` accessible
   authentication, `WCAG-3.2.6` consistent help, `WCAG-3.3.7` redundant entry). For
   `WCAG-2.5.8` target size (24×24 CSS px) also evaluate the spacing, equivalent control, inline,
   user-agent and essential exceptions; do not fail a small target without checking them.
   Tag accessibility cases `a11y`.
8. Localization: language switch, date/currency/decimal format (1.234,56 vs 1,234.56), Turkish
   characters (İ/ı, Ş/ş) in search and sorting.

Security cases are tagged with OWASP WSTG codes (for example `WSTG-SESS-01`); WSTG is a test
method guide, not a product rule.

Configuration coverage: apply pairwise to browser × viewport × language × role with the values in
the options block and source, as `config_matrix` (common rules; no rows, no copied cases).
Keep tests isolated; third-party services are stubbed or mocked (state the need).
Selectors: only when the options block names an automation tool, suggest role/label/data-testid
based selectors in `automation_open_points`; otherwise suggest none.

Özet: Kampanyalı sepet ve sipariş onayı

AC5: Sipariş onaylandığında sipariş numarası gösterilir ve sipariş, sipariş geçmişinde listelenir.
AC6: Kampanyalı siparişlerde minimum sipariş tutarı şartı aranmaz.

Platform ekleri (Testing Probe kuralları; talimattır, veri bloğu değildir). Ekler bir kontrol listesidir, case kotası değildir:

### Platform eki: platform-common@v1 (sha256:dd8c3c410250)
These rules apply to every platform section below. They extend the case rules; they never
override the source rules (no invented rule, message, code, threshold or timing).

- **Checklist, not quota.** The categories in a platform section are a checklist ([ISTQB]
  checklist-based testing, technique `CL`). Write a case only for a category that is relevant to
  the story and carries risk. Such a case gets a checklist coverage item `CL-n` whose definition
  names the category and, when there is one, the standard clause (for example
  `Web:Erişilebilirlik — klavyeyle tamamlama (WCAG-2.1.1)`, `Web:Girdi güvenliği — SQL
  enjeksiyonu (WSTG-INPV-05)`); the case lists `CL` in `technique` and the item in `covers`
  (together with the EP/BVA/… items whose input it uses). For a category you skip, add one
  `not_covered` entry (`item`: `<Web|Mobil|Desktop|API|Data>:<category>`, at most 40 characters,
  for example `Web:Responsive`, `Mobil:Kesintiler`) with the reason ("story has no …") and
  `question_ref` (the open question when the category waits for an answer, otherwise `null`). Do not
  write one case per category to fill the list. The limits stay: at most 15 cases per story and
  8 steps per case.
- **Category tags.** An accessibility case gets the tag `a11y`; a security case (authentication,
  authorization, injection, session, sensitive data) gets the tag `security`; a case with a
  measured time or load target from the source gets `performance`.
- **Values in the sections are placeholders.** Numbers in a platform section (versions, sizes,
  durations, breakpoints) are examples. A value becomes an expected result only when the story, an
  acceptance criterion, a PO answer, the analyst options block or an adopted standard states it.
- **Adopted standards.** The analyst options block has a line `Benimsenen standartlar:`. Only the
  standards listed there are adopted by the product. A threshold or rule from an adopted standard
  may be an expected result; put its id in the case's `standard_refs` (for example `WCAG-2.4.11`,
  `MASVS-STORAGE-1`, `API1:2023`, `WACK-CleanInstall`). A rule from a standard or platform guideline
  that is NOT listed (or the line says `yok`) is never an expected result: report it in
  `observations` (`standard_ref` + one-sentence `note`) and do not call it passed or failed. A
  non-adopted threshold you mention anywhere else in the output also appears in `observations`. You
  may still tag a case with a non-adopted standard id in `standard_refs` when the case's expected
  result comes from the source itself.
- **Support matrix.** When the options block does not give the browsers, OS versions or devices
  the product supports, do not choose them yourself: record an open question about the product's
  support policy (owner `PO`).
- **Configuration coverage.** When a platform section asks for pairwise configuration coverage,
  fill `config_matrix` with the parameters and their values (`parameters`) and the constraints
  between them (`constraints`, for example `IF Platform = "iOS" THEN Browser = "Safari"`). Do NOT
  write combination rows: a tool generates them from this model. Do not copy cases per
  combination; the functional cases run in every row. Use only values given in the options block
  or the source; when values are missing, leave the parameter out and record an open question.
- **Platform field.** `platform` is the platform the case is specific to (one of the selected
  platforms), or `null` when the case is platform-independent. When two platforms behave
  differently, write separate cases with their own `platform`.
- **Real device.** Set `requires_real_device: true` only for a case that cannot be verified on an
  emulator, simulator or virtual machine (camera, sensors, biometrics, real cellular network,
  battery, incoming call). Otherwise `false`.
- **Testability gaps.** When the story or options name a control that has no stable automation
  identity known to you, add a `testability_gaps` entry (`control`, `missing`: `AutomationId`,
  `accessible_name` or `test_id`) only if the options block names an automation tool; otherwise
  list the need in `automation_open_points`. Never invent selectors, locators or ids.
- **Test-type rules.** Performance: without load, data size, concurrency, a time target and a
  measurement environment in the source, write no threshold; ask for the missing values as open
  questions. Compatibility: without a support matrix, the support policy is an open question.
  Accessibility: keyboard-only flow, focus order, accessible name/role/state; the target level is
  the product's (adopted standards line). Security: only in a permitted test environment with
  synthetic data; attack text only in `test_data` with `is_attack_payload: true`; expected result
  is the rejection or non-disclosure the source supports.

### Platform eki: platform-api@v1 (sha256:05ca86c0cac3)
Platform: API / backend. Web, mobile and desktop clients share these services, so business rules
are cheapest to verify here. Input: the API contract in the options block line
`API sözleşmesi (OpenAPI/endpoint tanımı)` (when `API sözleşmesi var: evet` but no contract text
is given, record an open question that the contract is missing) and `Kimlik doğrulama tipi`.
When a contract is given, relate each case to its operation/schema. A response code or field that
is not in the contract or the story is never written as a requirement: open question.

For each endpoint the story touches, consider these categories (checklist, not quota; each
category you test is a `CL-n` item, common rules):

1. Schema validation (EP+BVA): per field type, required/optional, null, empty string, min/max,
   value outside the enum, unknown extra field, missing nested object, array with 0/1/max/max+1
   items (limits only from the contract/story).
2. HTTP semantics: the status codes defined in the contract, wrong method, wrong Content-Type,
   missing/broken JSON, large payload.
3. Identity and authorization: no token / expired / invalid signature / another user's resource
   (BOLA/IDOR), role × action decision table, privilege escalation.
4. Business rules (DT/ST): resource lifecycle (create → update → cancel), forbidden transitions.
5. Concurrency: parallel PUT on the same record (optimistic lock / ETag), race that exceeds a limit.
6. Paging and filters: page = 0/1/last/last+1, size = 0/1/max/max+1, invalid sort field.
7. Resilience: dependent service timeout/5xx, partial failure.
8. Data security: no stack trace or SQL in error responses, PII masking, injection.

Idempotency, retry, rate limit and timeout behaviour are expected results ONLY when the contract or
an acceptance criterion states them; otherwise open question.
For each case write the request (method, path, headers, body) in the steps and the expected
response (status, body schema, critical field values, side effect: DB / queue / log) in the
expected results, with `verification_point` `API` (or `DB`/`event`/`log` for the side effect).
Relevant OWASP API Security Top 10 2023 items go to `standard_refs` (`API1:2023` BOLA: another
user's id; `API3:2023` BOPLA: updating a field the role may not change; `API4:2023` resource
consumption: only at a defined limit). The list is an awareness checklist, not a product rule.
Keep the cases translatable to the automation tool in the options block (REST Assured, Postman,
Karate, pytest); without a tool, write no code.

### Platform eki: platform-web@v1 (sha256:eca203ba252e)
Platform: Web. Web-specific risks are browser behaviour, session, URL and multiple tabs. Targets
come from the options block lines `Tarayıcılar` and `Çözünürlükler`; when they are missing, the
support policy is an open question (common rules). Test what the user sees; do not depend on
implementation details such as CSS classes.

Besides the functional cases, consider these categories for the story (checklist, not quota;
each category you test is a `CL-n` item, common rules):

1. Browser behaviour: Back/Forward, page refresh in the middle of a form, double click / double
   submit, autofill, copy-paste.
2. Session and state: session timeout (only when the source gives the duration; [ISTQB]
   two-value BVA: timeout and timeout+1 s, with `BVA kipi: 3-değer` also timeout-1 s), the same
   record edited in two tabs, Back after logout, cleared cookies/localStorage, "remember me".
3. URL and authorization: direct URL to a page the role may not open, changing an id in the URL
   (IDOR), query parameter manipulation, login redirect after a deep link.
4. Responsive: breakpoints defined in the design (for example 767/768 px for a 768 px breakpoint;
   769 px only with `BVA kipi: 3-değer`), zoom 200 %, horizontal scrolling. Only breakpoints the
   source or options give.
5. Input security (permitted test environment only): XSS, SQL injection, HTML injection, very long
   input, Unicode/emoji/RTL text, leading/trailing spaces. Attack text only in `test_data` with
   `is_attack_payload: true`. Put the payload into a field whose rejection the source defines
   (for example a wrong password) so the expected result is the source's (no login, the AC's
   error, no SQL/stack trace in the response); tag `security`.
6. Network: slow connection, connection lost during a request, the UI on a 500/503/timeout
   response, loading state and button lock. The UI reaction is an expected result only when the
   source states it; otherwise open question.
7. Accessibility: keyboard-only completion, focus order, screen reader labels, error message tied
   to its field (aria-describedby), contrast. Tag with WCAG 2.2 criterion numbers (for example
   `WCAG-2.4.11` focus not obscured, `WCAG-2.5.7` dragging alternative, `WCAG-3.3.8` accessible
   authentication, `WCAG-3.2.6` consistent help, `WCAG-3.3.7` redundant entry). For
   `WCAG-2.5.8` target size (24×24 CSS px) also evaluate the spacing, equivalent control, inline,
   user-agent and essential exceptions; do not fail a small target without checking them.
   Tag accessibility cases `a11y`.
8. Localization: language switch, date/currency/decimal format (1.234,56 vs 1,234.56), Turkish
   characters (İ/ı, Ş/ş) in search and sorting.

Security cases are tagged with OWASP WSTG codes (for example `WSTG-SESS-01`); WSTG is a test
method guide, not a product rule.

Configuration coverage: apply pairwise to browser × viewport × language × role with the values in
the options block and source, as `config_matrix` (common rules; no rows, no copied cases).
Keep tests isolated; third-party services are stubbed or mocked (state the need).
Selectors: only when the options block names an automation tool, suggest role/label/data-testid
based selectors in `automation_open_points`; otherwise suggest none.
